name: Book Discussion | ‘A Moving Line’: Evolving Identities in Comics and Graphic Narratives
description: Join us for the book discussion of  A Moving Line , a celebration of India’s rich history of visual storytelling. Comic creator and visual artists  Rahil Mohsin  and  Mia Jose  will be in conversation with designer  Kriti Monga  to reflect on how storytelling in graphic narratives have evolved over centuries and the many nuances and developments in it.  This will be followed by an interactive Q&A with the audience. Here are the details: Date:  31st October 2026, Sunday Time:  6:00 PM (seating begins at 5:45 PM) Venue:  Champaca Bookstore, Vasanth Nagar RSVP here  to register. About the book:   Stories, whether written or drawn, are always moving, reshaped by every generation that inherits and retells them. India has a long and rich history of visual storytelling, from temple walls and painted scrolls to comics, graphic novels and webcomics. Published by the Museum of Art and Photography,  A Moving Line  traces this history, revealing unexpected connections between works that are rarely considered together. The eight essays and eleven graphic narratives in this collection range from the timeless to the future-forward. Bringing together contributions by scholars, practitioners and artists, this book explores the many nuances and developments in sequential storytelling. A Moving Line  celebrates a medium that has always been, and continues to be, inherently visual. Meet the speakers: Rahil Mohsin  is a Bengaluru-based comic creator and co-founder of  Hallubol , the world’s first bilingual Dakhni-English comic series, created alongside children’s book creator Alankrita Amaya. His portfolio includes work with Scout Comics, Comixense, Pratham Books, Sufi Comics, and Room to Read. Inspired by the everyday lives of working-class Muslim communities, his work explores the Dakhni language, folklore, culture, and food traditions of South India through graphic narratives rooted in multilingual realities. His stories often blend humour, memory, and voices rarely seen in contemporary comics. Mia Jose  (she/they) is a trans visual artist, art director, researcher and devourer of all things camp and horror. After transitioning from an active legal practice, she now uses graphic narratives to probe questions of gender, inheritance and embodiment, informed by her identity and roots in Kerala. Her creative practice is tied to her research on visual narrative traditions in India, and she is especially interested in the emergence of comics as vehicles for queer and marginalised voices. Having published several comics of her own, she is currently splitting her time between a short comic on mental health through monsters and folklore, and a graphic novel exploring masculinity and insecurity in the context of her hometown. Meet the moderator: Kriti Monga  brings over two decades of design experience to her multi-disciplinary practice, blending artistic expression, strategic design, and hands-on craftsmanship. The founder-director of the acclaimed Turmeric Design, her work spans brand building, book design, visual art, illustration, and mentorship. She also teaches professional design and typography programs globally. RSVP to reserve your spot.

name: Brunch & Books for Kids: Read-Aloud of ‘Manvinder’s Medu Vada’
description: Crispy, golden-brown, fluffy and white . . . who will make the perfect  medu vadas  for Manvinder? Come, join us for a yummy brunch for your little one and you, followed by a read-aloud session of  Manvinder’s Medu Vada,  written by Riddhi Maniar Doda and illustrated by Vinayak Sharma. The read-aloud session, conducted by SkilLit Readers, will be followed by a clay modeling activity where kids will make a food item they would like to eat.  Here are the details: Date:   10th October 2026, Saturday Time:  11:00 AM to 12:30 PM  Venue:  Champaca Bookstore, Indiranagar Age group:  4-7 years RSVP here  to register. The brunch menu curated by Copper + Cloves includes: The ticket price includes brunch for 1 child and 1 adult.  About the book: It is Manvinder’s first time eating a Medu vada in Bengaluru, and lo, behold, he is instantly hooked to the fluffy, crunchy ball of goodness! Manvinder refuses to eat anything else and the whole family leaves no stone unturned trying to recreate the Medu vada. Written by Riddhi Maniar Doda,  Manvinder's Medu Vada  is all about that hilarious struggle.  About SkillLit Readers: SkilLit Readers  is a story-led skills lab that uses books as launchpads to build independent thought and creative expression. They run book exploration programs that enable participants to think critically and connect with stories and their lives meaningfully. They strongly believe that reading is more than decoding the page and we use a range of experiential tools to bring books and stories to life. RSVP to reserve your spot.

name: Book Launch | ‘A Compendium of Supernatural Entities Found in the Government Girls Higher Secondary School’ by Kuzhali Manickavel
description: Join us for the book launch of  Kuzhali Manickavel's  debut novel  A Compendium of Supernatural Entities Found in the Government Girls Higher Secondary School , which draws from her high school years in small-town Tamil Nadu.  Her unique writing style includes elements of surrealism, horror, and unhinged humour; but much of her short fiction is also very grounded in a sense of place. In this talk, celebrated children's author  Shalini Srinivasan  will dialogue with Kuzhali about childhood visions, coming-of-age stories, and the monsters that haunt our dreams.   This will be followed by an interactive Q&A with the audience. Here are the details: Date:  11th October 2026, Sunday Time:  6:00 PM (seating begins at 5:45 PM) Venue:  Champaca Bookstore, Vasanth Nagar RSVP here  to register. About the book:  In the oppressive heat of a small Tamil Nadu town, bizarre happenings are common. And the local government secondary school is teeming with supernatural entities.  For Thamarai, an outsider considered strange by her peers, life is dreary and frustrating. She endures nosy neighbours and incomprehensible tuition classes. She despises the way her lecherous English teacher harasses the other girls in her grade. But when Thamarai finds a mysterious notebook full of descriptions of the school's paranormal phenomena, she wonders if it may hold the key to escape... Meet the author: Kuzhali Manickavel  was born in Winnipeg, Manitoba, and currently lives in Bangalore. She is the author of three collections of short fiction and several zines. This is her debut novel.  About the moderator:  Shalini Srinivasan  writes comics, picture books, and speculative fiction for children and adults. Her books include  Vanamala  and the  Cephalopod, Shoecat Thoocat  and most recently, the young adult fantasy,  A Forest Calls . She teaches at Azim Premji University, and spends a lot of time holding forth at captive students. RSVP to reserve your spot.

name: Book Launch | ‘Peace in the Land of the Dead’: Stories from the Hills of Manipur by Lian Dousel
description: Jobeth Warjri   engages  Lian Dousel  in conversation about the horror and the human in Lian’s  debut collection,  Peace in the Land of the Dead . In the twelve genre-bending stories, Dousel  plays with folktales, magic realism and horror, infusing them into the mundane.  Join us for this conversation where Warjri will examine the spectrum of genres and emotions Dousel has touched upon, his processes and inspirations, and what lies in the southern hills of Manipur.  This will be followed by an interactive Q&A with the audience. Here are the details: Date:  10th October 2026, Saturday Time:  6:00 PM (seating begins at 5:45 PM) Venue:  Champaca Bookstore, Vasanth Nagar RSVP here  to register. About the book:  In this debut collection, Lian Dousel carries you to the edges of Manipur, acquainting you with the quotidian lives of a people India knows little of, with folktales deeply embedded into the land. The stories are equally surreal and gritty, layered with a tinge of horror here and a tide of emotion there. Our protagonists encounter demons that decide their fate and hear laments of sentient woodlands, wonder what if and find out too late; they confront us with the fragility and endurance of human life. Meet the author: Lian Dousel  is a writer from Lamka, Manipur. He has a master’s degree in Literary Art from Ambedkar University, Delhi. His fiction has appeared in various outlets such as  Hammock, The Little Journal of Northeast India , and  Lekha Writers .  Peace in the Land of the Dead   is his debut collection. He is currently based in Delhi. About the moderator:  Jobeth Ann Warjri   is a writer, teacher and researcher from Laitkor, Meghalaya. She is the  editor of the anthology,  The Greatest Stories from the Northeast Ever Told   and the winner of The Book Review Literary Trust Short Story Competition 2020. She lives in Bangalore where she teaches writing at the School of Liberal Arts and Sciences at Vidyashilp University. RSVP to reserve your spot.

name: Book Launch | ‘Powering the Future’ by Neha Saigal, with Nirmala Raja & Md. Ainul
description: India’s energy transition is not just about moving from coal to renewables — it is about who gets to shape that future.  As part of India Climate Week, join author  Neha Saigal  in conversation with  Nirmala Raja  and  Md. Ainul  as they explore what a truly just and inclusive energy transition looks like on the ground — from women-led environmental action and community livelihoods to the realities of coal-affected communities. Drawing on stories from across India, the conversation will ask what it takes to put women, communities and lived realities at the heart of our energy future from the book  Powering the Future . This will be followed by an interactive Q&A with the audience. Here are the details: Date:  3rd October 2026, Saturday Time:  4:00 PM (seating begins at 3:45 PM) Venue:  Champaca Bookstore, Vasanth Nagar RSVP here to register. About the book:  What does India’s energy transition look like when seen through the lives of women shaping it every day? Powering the Future   travels across Odisha, Maharashtra, Punjab, Jharkhand, and Tamil Nadu to tell stories of women at the centre of change as entrepreneurs powering rural livelihoods with solar energy, innovators rethinking clean cooking, civic leaders advancing electric mobility, communities facing the uncertainties of coal, and women bringing care and equity into institutions and policy. These are not only stories of clean energy, but of dignity, work, health, resilience, and hope. At a time when India is rapidly reimagining its energy future, this publication invites readers to look beyond targets and technologies, and to recognise the women whose leadership is already lighting the way. Meet the author: Neha Saigal   is the author, CEO and co-founder of climate & care collective and the co-founder of intertidal lab. Neha’s work focuses on the intersections of ecology, feminism and regenerative economies. Her work involves working closely with leaders who are reimagining futures rooted in care during this time of polycrisis. About the speakers:  Nirmala Raja  is the Chairperson of Ramco Community Services, where she oversees initiatives spanning education, mental health, environmental restoration and community development. She is also the Managing Director of Rajapalayam Mills Limited. A Board Member of Arsha Vidya Mandir and the Indian Schools Debating Society, she has been closely involved in the development of Arsha Vidya Mandir since its establishment in 2002. She currently serves on the Tamil Nadu Governing Council on Climate Change. Md. Ainul  is a grassroots activist from Taitulya village in Dhanbad, Jharkhand. His work brings communities together around issues of water, forests, land and people’s rights, including the Right to Education, Right to Information, Forest Rights Act and Right to Food. He was also one of the key organisers of the campaign to clean and protect the Damodar River, a lifeline for Jharkhand, combining grassroots mobilisation with efforts to build greater awareness about the river and its importance to local communities. About the organisation: The  Climate & Care Collective  works with communities at the frontlines of climate change to shape solutions for healthier ecosystems and stronger livelihoods. We create spaces for communities, practitioners and researchers to come together, share knowledge and imagine more just, collaborative futures. RSVP here to register .
